question.problem:
Let $B$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and let $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ be a linear transformation. Find $[\,T\,]_{B}$, given that

$\,$ $T([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}x+3y \\ 2x-y\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}.$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}.$ The $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B.$

First, let's find the image of ${b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2}$ under $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1}) & =T([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2}) & =T([\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 7 & 3 \\ 2 & 2 & 0 & -8\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 7 & 3 \\ 0 & 8 & -14 & -14\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{8}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 7 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{7}{4} & -\frac{7}{4}\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{7}{4} & -\frac{9}{4} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{7}{4} & -\frac{7}{4}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{4} & -\frac{9}{4} \\ -\frac{7}{4} & -\frac{7}{4}\end{aligned}].
$$
